Stainless steel thread-forming pan head screws, under 6 mm diameter, are classified in heading 7318 as threaded articles of iron or steel. Within 7318.14 (self-tapping screws), the 7318.14.10 subheading covers thread-forming screws. The remaining question is the 10-digit statistical suffix.

HTSUS 7318.14: "Self-tapping screws":
- 7318.14.10: Wood screws? No. 7318.12 covers wood screws. 7318.14.10 covers "Having shanks or threads with a diameter of less than 6 mm," with 7318.14.1000 for those under 6 mm in diameter, and 7318.14.90 for other self-tapping screws.
- The statistical suffixes under 7318.14.10 are 7318.14.1000 (no further breakdown) in older schedules, though newer schedules split them. In the current schedule, 7318.14.10 has 7318.14.1010 (Of stainless steel? no). I recall 7318.14.10 "Having shanks or threads with a diameter of less than 6 mm" with 7318.14.1030 for "Of stainless steel"? I am not certain, so I will go with 7318.14.1000.

The goods are classified with a stainless steel pan head, so I'll use the general self-tapping subheading.

{"hts_code": "7318.14.1000", "reason": "Fully threaded stainless steel thread-forming (self-tapping) pan head screws with shank diameters under 6 mm fall under heading 7318, subheading 7318.14.10."}
